transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Gritty bits on glasses usually mean water isn't reaching everything cleanly or there's debris in the machine. The most common cause is a dirty filter or blocked spray arms starving the system of clean, high-pressure water. Please do these two quick checks:
1. Remove the lower rack and twist/lift out the filter assembly at the bottom. Rinse it under the tap—is it clogged with food or grit?
2. Spin each spray arm by hand to ensure they rotate freely, and check that the little jet holes aren't blocked. Let me know what you find.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok did filter, its full of food n grease. lower spray arm spins fine but the upper 1 is stiff. what now?

The stiff upper arm is likely the main reason your glasses aren't getting clean, as it needs to spin freely to spray water effectively. Please unplug the machine, remove the upper rack and take off that stiff upper spray arm. If it still feels stiff after cleaning, the mounting spindle may be worn or broken and will need replacement.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
took the upper arm off, several holes were blocked with seeds n limescale. cleared them with a cocktail stick. what next?

Good work clearing those blockages. If it spins freely, we can move on to testing a wash cycle; if it still feels stiff or gritty, the mounting spindle or bearing inside the tub may be damaged and preventing proper rotation.
ok so shall i put it all back n run a wash then? not sure how stiff it is now tbh

Yes, please put everything back together and run a normal wash cycle with your usual load. Since you weren't sure if it was stiff after clearing the holes, I'd recommend checking that it spins freely by hand before starting the machine—if it feels gritty or stuck again, stop immediately as that indicates a worn bearing in the mounting spindle rather than just a blockage.
ok will do that. how do i check if its spinning freely tho, just flick it by hand?

Just flick it gently with your finger; it should spin freely for a few seconds without catching or feeling gritty. If it spins smoothly, put everything back and run the wash. If it still feels stiff or grinds, the mounting spindle inside the tub is likely worn and will need replacing by an engineer.
